skill.description: Guides Claude Code plugin authors through Model Context Protocol server setup, transport selection, authentication, tool naming, testing, and troubleshooting.

security_audit.summary: All static findings were adjudicated as documentation or example configuration, not executable behavior. The reviewed files mention URLs, environment variable placeholders, and shell snippets, but no automatic command execution, credential exfiltration, or prompt injection text was found.

static_findings.snippet: Connect to RESTful MCP servers via standard HTTP requests. Best for token-based auth and stateless i
Use `/mcp` command to see all servers including plugin-provided ones.
- **`references/server-types.md`** - Deep dive on each server type
- **`references/tool-usage.md`** - Using MCP tools in commands and agents
2. Create `.mcp.json` at plugin root with configuration
- Claude Code spawns and manages the process

content.user_title: Build MCP Integrations for Claude Code
content.value_statement: MCP setup across transports, auth, and tool naming is easy to misconfigure. This skill guides Claude Code plugin authors through MCP server configuration and usage.
actual_capabilities: Explains .mcp.json and plugin.json MCP server configuration.
Compares stdio, SSE, HTTP, and WebSocket MCP server types.
Shows OAuth, bearer token, API key, and environment variable auth patterns.
Documents MCP tool naming and allowed-tools configuration for commands.
Provides example configurations for stdio, SSE, and HTTP MCP servers.
Lists troubleshooting checks for auth, connection, and tool discovery issues.
limitations: It does not install or run MCP servers by itself.
It does not verify remote service availability or credentials.
Example URLs and environment variables must be replaced before use.
Security depends on the scopes and permissions chosen by the plugin author.

use_cases.title: Add a Hosted MCP Server
use_cases.description: Configure an SSE or HTTP MCP endpoint with clear auth and setup notes.

use_cases.title: Review Local Server Configuration
use_cases.description: Check stdio server commands, environment variables, and portable plugin paths.

use_cases.title: Document MCP Tool Workflows
use_cases.description: Map MCP tool names into commands, agents, and troubleshooting guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic MCP Config
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add a basic MCP server to my Claude Code plugin. Ask which transport I need, then outline the configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Right Server Type
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare stdio, SSE, HTTP, and WebSocket for my plugin. Recommend one based on local execution, auth, latency, and setup needs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an authentication plan for my MCP integration. Cover OAuth, environment variables, token scopes, and user setup documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Multi-Server Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned multi-server MCP plugin architecture. Check server types, allowed tools, auth boundaries, error handling, and troubleshooting coverage.

output_examples.input: I need to connect a plugin to an HTTP API with a bearer token.
output: Recommended HTTP transport for stateless API calls.
Use an environment variable for the bearer token.
Document token scopes, setup steps, and common auth failures.

output_examples.input: My command needs to create and search tasks through an MCP server.
output: List only the specific MCP tools needed by the command.
Validate required user inputs before each tool call.
Return clear success, partial success, and failure messages.

output_examples.input: I want to support both local development and production endpoints.
output: Use environment variables for endpoint selection.
Prefer secure production URLs and scoped tokens.
Add troubleshooting steps for missing variables and failed connections.

best_practices: Use HTTPS or WSS for hosted MCP servers.
Pre-allow only the MCP tools each command actually needs.
Document every required environment variable and permission scope.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode tokens, API keys, or database credentials.
Do not use wildcard MCP tool access unless the workflow requires it.
Do not copy example URLs or placeholders into production unchanged.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you configure MCP servers for Claude Code plugins and document their tool usage.

faq.question: Does it create MCP server code?
faq.answer: It focuses on configuration, authentication patterns, and workflow guidance. It does not generate a complete server implementation by default.

faq.question: Which MCP transports are covered?
faq.answer: It covers stdio, SSE, HTTP, and WebSocket transports with practical selection guidance.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use environment variables or OAuth flows. Do not commit credentials in plugin files or examples.

faq.question: Can it help with Claude Code command permissions?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains MCP tool names and how to list specific allowed tools in commands.

faq.question: Is this only useful for Claude Code?
faq.answer: The guidance is written for Claude Code plugins, but many MCP configuration concepts also help Codex and Claude users.
